evidence.detail: PD.formatPercentage creates a new Intl.NumberFormat(...) object on every invocation rather than reusing a cached instance — MDN explicitly warns this pattern is inefficient for repeated calls
Format tick marks for percentages in a sane fashion — introduced PD.formatPercentage using Intl.NumberFormat but still constructs a new instance per call
formatPercentage is used as a Chart.js tick callback and tooltip formatter, meaning it is called once per data point per render — potentially dozens of times per chart

triage.fix_sketch: In shared_web/static/js/pd.js, extract the Intl.NumberFormat construction to a module-level constant: const PD_PERCENTAGE_FORMATTER = new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, { style: 'percent', minimumSignificantDigits: 2, maximumSignificantDigits: 2 }); then replace the new Intl.NumberFormat(...) inside formatPercentage with PD_PERCENTAGE_FORMATTER.format(value) — keeping the existing .replace() chain unchanged. 3-line net change.
triage.notes: The issue author noted 'It probably doesn't matter for the number of times we're going to do it' — this is a minor performance cleanup, not a correctness bug. Confidence is medium because commit 6d4583a2 may have been intended as the response to this issue even though it left the per-call construction in place.
